nonint.text: Noninterest Expense. Total noninterest expense increased $329 thousand, or 4.3%, to $8.0 million during the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $7.7 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, as reflected below (dollars in thousands):

nonop.heading: Interest Expense
nonop.text:
Q3 2026 vs Q3 2025 . Total interest expense decreased $724 thousand, or 12.7%, to $5.0 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, from $5.7 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The decrease was primarily attributable to lower interest rates across all interest-bearing liabilities excluding subordinated notes, resulting from lower market interest rates generally, and lower balances of both borrowings and subordinated notes partially offset by an increase in the rate paid on our subordinated debt.

Interest expense on certificate accounts declined $175 thousand, driven by a $203 thousand rate-related decrease, partially offset by a $28 thousand volume-related increase. The average balance of certificate accounts rose to $295.9 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, from $292.7 million for the same period in 2025, while the average rate paid fell to 3.53% from 3.80%. The decline in the average rate reflected lower market interest rates and the repricing of maturing certificates into the current rate environment. In addition, interest expense on demand and NOW accounts decreased $18 thousand, due to both lower average balances and slightly lower average rates.

tax.text: Income Tax Expense . The provision for income taxes was $584 thousand and $1.6 million for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $395 thousand and $1.2 million for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025, respectively. The effective tax rates for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 were 20.10% and 19.62%, compared to 18.90% and 19.30% for the same periods in 2025.

Net interest income.text: The efficiency ratio improved 285 basis points to 75.31% for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 from 78.16% for the same period in 2025, primarily reflecting modest growth in net interest income driven by lower funding costs and higher yields on interest-earning assets, and higher noninterest income.

Noninterest income.text: loans which conform to the underwriting standards of Fannie Mae (“conforming”) and retain the servicing of such loans in order to maintain the direct customer relationship and to generate noninterest income. Residential loans which do not conform to the underwriting standards of Fannie Mae (“non-conforming”) are either held in our loan portfolio or sold with servicing released. We originate and retain a significant amount of commercial real estate loans, including those secured by owner-occupied and nonowner-occupied commercial real estate, multifamily properties and mobile home parks, and construction and land development loans.
